dietEvidence.body: Herbivory is inferred from ankylosaur anatomy. The skull of Minmi is unknown, so its jaw apparatus and feeding style cannot be examined directly.

sizeNote: Length and mass are estimates from incomplete material, not measurements of a whole animal.
tagline: A small ankylosaur from Australia with a relatively long tail and extensive armour. Its phylogenetic position among ankylosaurs is debated.
summary: A small ankylosaur from Australia with a relatively long tail and extensive armour. Its phylogenetic position among ankylosaurs is debated.

discovery.body: Named by Molnar, 1980. The record is known from Bungil Formation, Queensland. A nearly complete skeleton with armour and some soft-tissue impressions.

fossilEvidence.title: Preserved material
fossilEvidence.body: The holotype, QM F10329, is a partial skeleton from the Bungil Formation near Roma, Queensland. It lacks a skull. The Allaru specimen formerly called Minmi sp. is Kunbarrasaurus ieversi.

fossilEvidence.title: Stratigraphic and geographic occurrence
fossilEvidence.body: Bungil Formation, Queensland records the species in the Early Cretaceous. The numeric range used here is ≈120–112 Ma, an occurrence estimate rather than a direct date on every specimen.

anatomy.title: Preserved anatomy
anatomy.body: The holotype preserves vertebrae, ribs, part of a hindlimb and armour, including the unusual paravertebral elements that give the species its name. The skull is unknown.

behaviour.body: No direct evidence of social or parental behaviour. The armour is preserved; its defensive function is inferred from structure and position.

reconstruction.body: A licensed life reconstruction is assigned to this record and credited in Sources and credits. The species is known from a nearly complete skeleton with armour and some soft-tissue impressions. The reconstruction is an artist's interpretation of appearance, not a direct observation from the fossil record; preserved integument, where present, is described in the anatomy section, and the soft-tissue outline is otherwise inferred.

confidenceNote: Minmi paravertebra is based on the holotype, QM F10329, a partial skeleton from the Bungil Formation that lacks a skull. The much more complete Allaru Mudstone skeleton formerly called Minmi sp. was named Kunbarrasaurus ieversi in 2015. The family placement of Minmi remains unresolved.

primer.lead: Minmi paravertebra was a small armoured dinosaur from the [Early Cretaceous](/deep-time?period=cretaceous) of Queensland, Australia. It belonged to Ankylosauria, the group with body armour and, in many species, a tail club.
paragraphs: The holotype, QM F10329, is a partial skeleton that lacks a skull. It preserves vertebrae, ribs, part of a hindlimb and armour, including the unusual paravertebral elements that give the species its name. A much more complete skeleton from the Allaru Mudstone was formerly called Minmi sp., but it was renamed Kunbarrasaurus ieversi in 2015.
Its plant diet is inferred from ankylosaur anatomy, not from its own skull. The family placement of Minmi is unresolved, and there is no direct evidence of its behaviour.
primer.takeaway: A small Australian ankylosaur known mainly from a skull-less partial skeleton.
